governing_policy: All V3.3 experiments must be pre-registered with frozen hypotheses, splits, and acceptance criteria before evaluation.

experiments.Hypothesis: A coverage factor k selected exclusively using calibration data maintains acceptable empirical coverage on previously unseen evaluation data drawn from the same declared ODD population without parameter re-tuning.
experiments.Treatment: Out-of-sample evaluation on independent unseen frames with locked k
experiments.EvaluationMethod: Closed-form elliptical boundary containment on independent test coordinates with Wilson score interval
experiments.AcceptanceCriteria: Nominal ODD empirical coverage >= 0.9500 with documented Wilson score 95% CI; separate reporting of calibration vs out-of-sample coverage
experiments.Interpretation: EXECUTED_WITH_LIMITATIONS: Factor k=2.42 locked on Sector B. On unseen nominal ODD data, coverage was 92.61% [95% CI: 90.36%-94.36%], revealing empirical undercoverage. Far-field (>8m) coverage fell to 67.07%, cataloged as V3.3-FAIL-001.

experiments.Hypothesis: Computer vision perception, tracking, and hazard detection maintain bounded degradation across diverse warehouse layouts, mounting geometries, and lighting conditions compared to the development baseline.
IndependentVariables: Layout (Wide aisle, High bay, T-intersection, Staging)
experiments.Control: Nominal baseline performance in Sector A main aisle
experiments.Treatment: Multi-environment cross-evaluation in Sectors B, C, and D
experiments.EvaluationMethod: Multi-strata perception matrix and non-parametric trajectory bootstrap CI for tracking IDF1
experiments.AcceptanceCriteria: Perception recall >= 0.85 across nominal strata; IDF1 >= 0.80 with trajectory bootstrap CI; zero silent failure under degraded conditions
experiments.Interpretation: EXECUTED: Evaluated across 4 warehouse sectors and 6 operational levels. Perception F1 achieved 88.45%; Tracking IDF1 achieved 91.80% [95% CI: 90.57%-92.95%]; Hazard recall achieved 94.12%.

experiments.Hypothesis: Rigorous two-zone Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with pre-treatment trend validation distinguishes genuine safety improvements from safety backfire (risk redistribution, new hazard creation) and refuses attribution (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) when parallel trends fail.
IndependentVariables: Intervention topology (barrier, speed limiter, detour routing, staging relocation)
experiments.Treatment: Treated intervention zone with physical modification
experiments.EvaluationMethod: Two-zone Difference-in-Differences with pre-treatment trend slope equality test and backfire taxonomy classification
experiments.AcceptanceCriteria: Correct classification across taxonomy (RISK_REDUCED, RISK_REDISTRIBUTED, PARTIAL_BACKFIRE, NEW_HAZARD_CREATED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE); zero causal claims under parallel-trend failure
experiments.Interpretation: EXECUTED: Expanded empirical intervention evidence from N=2 to N=5. Accurately identified RISK_REDISTRIBUTED (barrier, staging), RISK_REDUCED (speed limiter), NEW_HAZARD_CREATED (detour), and successfully refused attribution (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) under exogenous shock.

experiments.Hypothesis: Automated boundary gating triggers SAFE_REFUSAL_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when input telemetry falls outside the ODD (slope > 1.5 deg, distance > 8.0m, latency > 500ms, extreme occlusion) rather than executing unsafe intervention decisions.
experiments.Control: Standard open-loop baseline without telemetry gating
experiments.Treatment: Closed-loop SafeRefusalEngine with multi-modal boundary gating
experiments.EvaluationMethod: Multi-modal boundary gate stress testing and 10 adversarial red-team operational scenarios
experiments.AcceptanceCriteria: Appropriate refusal rate >= 0.98 on out-of-ODD inputs; unsafe non-refusal rate <= 0.01; false refusal rate <= 0.05 on nominal inputs
experiments.Interpretation: EXECUTED: Achieved 100% appropriate refusal rate on out-of-ODD violations, 0.0% unsafe non-refusal rate, and 0.0% false refusal rate under nominal conditions. 10 red-team scenarios cataloged.
